🇺🇸 TRUMP: U.S. COURT BACKS END OF “DE MINIMIS” DUTY-FREE IMPORT EXEMPTION

• ⚖️ Trump says the U.S. Court of International Trade ruled the President had legal authority to end the de minimis exemption

• 📦 Earlier, foreign shipments valued up to $800 could enter the U.S. duty-free

• 🚫 The exemption has now been closed, meaning low-value foreign shipments no longer automatically escape tariffs

• 💰 Trump claims the exemption resulted in an estimated $10.8 billion of foregone tariff revenue in 2024

• 🏭 Move aims to protect U.S. manufacturers/workers, increase tariff collections and tighten scrutiny of imported goods

• 🌎 Impact: Negative for foreign exporters and cross-border e-commerce sellers relying heavily on low-value shipments to the U.S.; potentially positive for competing U.S. manufacturers.

• 🔋 Offers 179 km certified range with a 9.2 kWh battery.

• ⚡ Fast charging enables 0–80% charge in ~2 hours 30 minutes.

• 📱 Equipped with TVS SmartXonnect, providing real-time navigation, vehicle alerts and diagnostics.

• 🛡️ Comes with a 6-year warranty and will be available across Sri Lanka by September 2026.

🟢 Impact: Positive — Launch expands TVS Motor’s EV footprint in Sri Lanka and strengthens its presence in the electric three-wheeler market.

CDSL ; CO TO INVEST ADDITIONAL ₹5 CR IN ONDC

• 📈 CDSL has received SEBI approval to make a further investment of up to ₹5 Cr in Open Network for Digital Commerce (ONDC).

• 💵 Investment will be through subscription to 5 lakh equity shares at ₹100 per share, in one or more tranches.

• 📊 CDSL currently holds 1.85% stake in ONDC; after the proposed investment, its stake will reduce to approximately 1.67% due to dilution.

• 🏦 CDSL’s existing investment in ONDC stands at around ₹20.29 Cr.

• 🤝 Investment is described as strategic and is not a related-party transaction.

🟢 Impact: Positive — Further investment strengthens CDSL’s strategic participation in India’s growing digital commerce infrastructure, though the ₹5 Cr investment is relatively small.

GANESHA ECOSPHERE REPORTS FIRE AT WARANGAL POLYESTER STAPLE FIBER PLANT

• 🏭 Fire occurred at the Polyester Staple Fiber (PSF) plant of wholly owned subsidiary Ganesha Ecopet in Warangal, Telangana.

• 🚒 Fire was brought under control with the plant’s safety team and local fire authorities.

• ⚠️ Operations in the affected area are temporarily disrupted; damage assessment is underway.

• ✅ Other divisions — B2B Chips, Filament Yarn, PPSF and Washline — remain unaffected and are operating normally.

• 🛡️ Assets are adequately insured and the insurer has been informed.

🔴 Impact: Negative — Temporary disruption at the PSF plant may affect operations, though insurance coverage and unaffected operations at other divisions limit the impact.

🟡 Impact: Neutral — Provides additional funding for business requirements, but the relatively small loan size limits the overall financial impact.

MANORAMA INDUSTRIES Q1 : EXPANDS WEST AFRICA SOURCING PRESENCE

• 📈 Q1 FY27 revenue grew 39.5% YoY, crossing the ₹400 Cr quarterly revenue milestone for the first time.

• 💰 Profitability increased 67.6% YoY, supported by strong demand and higher contribution from value-added specialty fats & butters.

• 🇹🇩 Incorporated wholly owned subsidiary Manorama Savannah Agro Chad SARL to strengthen Shea sourcing in Chad.

• 🏭 Acquired ~10 hectares (24 acres) of land in Burkina Faso for a Shea seed processing facility; regulatory approvals are underway.

• 💵 Successful QIP completion strengthens the balance sheet and provides funding flexibility for manufacturing, sourcing and value-added product expansion.

🟢 Impact: Positive — Strong Q1 growth, deeper West African sourcing integration and expansion initiatives improve supply security and support long-term growth.

SAATVIK GREEN ENERGY SECURES ₹132 CR SOLAR MODULE ORDER

• ⚡ Order involves the supply of Solar PV Modules.

• 🏭 Order received from a renowned Independent Power Producer/EPC player.

• 🇮🇳 The order is domestic in nature.

• 📅 Order execution is scheduled by January 2027.

🟢 Impact: Positive — ₹132 Cr order strengthens the company’s order book and provides near-term revenue visibility.

IXIGO TO SELL 17.39% STAKE IN FRESHBUS FOR ~₹36.6 CR

• 🚌 Ixigo will sell 46,264 preference shares of Freshbus to Twelve Stone LLP at ₹7,911 per share.

• 💵 Total cash consideration stands at approximately ₹36.6 Cr.

• 📉 Ixigo’s stake in Freshbus will reduce from 25.66% to 8.27% of paid-up share capital.

• 🔄 Following the transaction, Freshbus will cease to be an associate company of Ixigo.

• 📊 Ixigo had originally acquired Freshbus shares at ₹2,344 per share in 2022, implying a significant appreciation in investment value.

• 📅 Transaction is expected to be completed on or before August 30, 2026.

🟢 Impact: Positive — Ixigo monetises part of its Freshbus investment at a substantially higher price while retaining an 8.27% stake.

VESUVIUS INDIA TO SELL MEHSANA FACILITY TO FOSECO INDIA FOR ₹43.25 CR

• 🏭 Vesuvius India approved the sale of its Mehsana manufacturing facility in Gujarat to Foseco India.

• 💵 Transaction value stands at ₹43.25 Cr, on a slump-sale basis.

• 📊 Mehsana facility contributed ₹58.13 Cr revenue and ₹34.74 Cr net worth in CY2025.

• 🔥 Facility primarily manufactures crucibles, stoppers and sleeves for the non-ferrous industrial sector.

• 🤝 Foseco India is part of the same Vesuvius Group, making this a related-party transaction; the company states it will be carried out at arm’s length.

• 📅 Transaction is expected to be completed by December 31, 2026.

🟡 Impact: Neutral — Sale monetises a non-core foundry-related business while transferring it to the group's specialist non-ferrous foundry platform.

• 💰 Operating EBITDA stood at ₹298.6 Cr, down 7% YoY; EBITDA/tonne at ₹784.

• 📈 Investment is expected to support business growth and enhance the subsidiary’s long-term value.

• 💵 Capital infusion will be through cash consideration in one or more tranches, based on funding requirements.

• 📅 Infusion is expected to be completed by March 31, 2027.

🟢 Impact: Positive — Strengthens Jet Freight’s US expansion strategy and supports growth in its international logistics business.

Sansera builds precision metal parts for cars, planes, and chip-making machines. Its aerospace and semiconductor order book jumped to Rs 5750 crore from Rs 4464 crore in 3 months, after winning Rs 1250 crore deal from single semiconductor equipment maker. 

That customer builds machines used inside chip factories. Global spending on such machines crossed $143B in 2026 because AI needs more chips than factories can produce. 

Sansera machines complex metal chambers these factories require. Revenue from this deal starts in 2027 and peaks in 2029. >>

Non-auto sales more than doubled. EBITDA margin improved to 19.2% from 17.2%, means company kept more of each rupee earned. 

Aerospace and semiconductor work brought in Rs 315 crore last year and targets Rs 550-600 crore this year. Company appointed separate CEO just for this segment, treating it as independent operation. 

This work earns 25-30% margins versus 19% company average. As it grows, blended profitability rises without needing price hikes.

They can now machine turbine blisks and single-crystal metal parts, skills very few companies globally have. Blisks are rotating discs with blades attached, used inside jet engines. 

Making them requires cutting titanium or nickel alloys to extreme precision. Single-crystal parts are harder because metal has no grain boundaries, so conventional cutting fails. 

These capabilities move Sansera from making seat brackets and cargo parts to engine-level aerospace components where margins and barriers run far higher. 

New hangar and facility under construction, targeting Rs 8000-9000 crore revenue by decade end.

- Focus includes US market opportunity.

Balance Sheet
- Net Debt: ₹42,200 Cr.
- Free Cash Flow: -₹11,800 Cr.
- Negative FCF remains key concern.
- Balance-sheet deleveraging requires monitoring.

Management Outlook
- Domestic demand expected to remain healthy.
- EV penetration remains supportive.
- New launches expected to drive growth.
- Revenue growth remains key focus.
- Cost reduction initiatives continue.
- Calibrated pricing actions planned.
- Supply constraints targeted for resolution.
- Commodity costs expected to remain elevated.

Key Positives
- Domestic PV revenue grew 65%.
- Healthy domestic demand environment.
- Rising EV penetration supports growth.
- New launches provide growth potential.
- Strong premium JLR product mix.
- Four new BEVs expected.
- Significant JLR cost-saving opportunity.

Key Concerns
- Sharp PAT decline.
- EBITDA margin compressed significantly.
- JLR revenue declined 10%.
- JLR profitability weakened.
- Negative consolidated FCF.
- Net debt remains elevated.
- Commodity costs remain high.
- Geopolitical risks persist.

Key Monitorables
- Domestic PV volumes.
- EV penetration.
- New model launches.
- JLR BEV launches.
- JLR wholesale volumes.
- JLR EBIT margin.

- FCF improvement.

Impact
- Mixed to Negative.
- Domestic PV performance remains strong.
- Consolidated profitability weakened sharply.
- JLR remains the major drag.
- Margin recovery is critical.
- New launches provide medium-term upside.

Key Takeaway
- Tata Motors PV delivered a mixed Q1FY27, with domestic PV revenue growing strongly by 65% but consolidated profitability declining sharply due to weaker JLR performance, supply disruptions, geopolitical issues and elevated costs. Revenue beat estimates, while EBITDA and margins missed expectations. Healthy domestic demand, rising EV penetration and upcoming JLR BEV launches provide growth opportunities, but margin recovery, FCF improvement, JLR execution and debt reduction remain the key monitorables.

Unihealth Hospitals achieves another clinical milestone in Advanced Minimally Invasive Surgery

Unihealth Hospitals Limited (NSE Emerge: UNIHEALTH) announces that UMC Hospitals, Navi Mumbai, has successfully treated a 33-year-old patient with a large walled-off pancreatic necrosis, a serious delayed complication following severe pancreatitis.

The complex case was successfully managed by Dr. Harsh Sheth, Consultant Bariatric & GI Laparoscopic Surgeon, using an advanced laparoscopic minimally invasive approach, avoiding the need for a conventional large open surgery. 

This achievement further strengthens UMC Hospitals, Navi Mumbai’s capabilities in Gastrointestinal, Laparoscopic and Pancreatic Surgery, and adds to its growing portfolio of advanced clinical interventions.

In recent months, UMC Hospitals has achieved several notable milestones, including Robotic Knee Replacement, IVUS-guided Cardiac Intervention and Navi Mumbai’s 1st Bilateral Robotic Direct Anterior Approach Total Hip Replacement.
